title: Channel listing preflight + demo flow (partner-facing slate)
content:
Purpose:
- Quick preflight + demo flow to validate technical and copy readiness before partner publish to cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, GCP).
- This doc is a hybrid checklist + partner-facing demo script we expect Solutions Engineers (SEs) to use during final partner sign-off.

Audience:
- Primary: Partner PMs/SEs, Redwood Solutions Eng, Marketplace ops.
- Secondary: Legal (for final billing/KMS clauses), Docs for tile copy finalization.

High-level entry criteria (must be green before demo):
- SKU mapped to billing meter (billing owner verified)
- Legal banner & trial terms approved by legal@ (ticket GTM-LEGAL-210)
- Images/tiles uploaded to vendor portal and signed off (PR #58)
- Automated provisioning route returns 200 and provisions a sample trial within 5 mins
- SSO + SAML test account validated (if partner requires SSO)

Preflight checklist (tech + ops) — run during dry-run and again in demo:
1) SKU & Metering
   - SKU slug assigned and matches Go-to-Market mapping spreadsheet (col D).
   - Metering event names: token_generate, embed_call, rerank_call — confirm mapping to marketplace meter IDs.
   - Metering sample logs show event -> meter id mapping in last 24h.

2) Provisioning & Trial
   - Provision API endpoint: POST /provision returns {status: "ok", instance_id: ...} within 2x SLA.
   - Trial provisioning completes end-to-end, test runs 3 sample generations.
   - Trial expires & transitions to paid state; subscription flow hits billing webhook.

3) Security & Compliance
   - KMS key alias configured for tenant (if using dedicated/private).
   - PII isolation: demo tenant data persists <72h; confirmed by infra.
   - Audit logs accessible and validated for one sample request.

4) UX/Listing copy + assets
   - 60-char short title approved.
   - 300-char short description (marketing elevator) and 1500-char long description (technical + use cases).
   - Feature bullets (5) and 3 sample prompts + responses for tile.
   - Tiles/screenshots uploaded; alt text present.

5) Docs & Support
   - Quickstart guide URL (pointing to a dedicated listing-runbook) is live.
   - Support contact (support@redwood.ai) and SLA snippet present in listing.

6) Billing & Legal
   - Marketplace SKU entitlements match the internal pricebook.
   - Legal-approved trial terms & refund policy copy baked into listing.

7) Regional & Capacity gating
   - Regions targeted: us-east-1, eu-west-1 initially.
   - Capacity plan: dedicated pool <-> fallback to hosted at 5% buffer.
   - Failover route tested (simulate dedicated pool OOM).

Partner-facing demo flow (30-min session) — oriented for SE to run with partner PM/SE
- 0:00 — Quick intro (3m): Goal: verify listing + provisioning + billing signals.
- 3:00 — Listing walkthrough (5m): Read short title + tile copy out loud; show screenshots.
- 8:00 — Provisioning (10m): Initiate provisioning from marketplace product tile; show provisioning webhook flows in console.
   + Verify token issuance and sample inference (3 short queries).
- 18:00 — Billing signal check (4m): Trigger a billable usage event; verify metering event appears in marketplace test console and internal logs.
- 22:00 — Failover test (5m): Simulate constrained capacity -> verify automatic fallback route serves requests within degraded latency SLA.
- 27:00 — Wrap + Next steps (3m): Confirm partner acceptance checklist, finalize publish ticket.

Copy variants (short + long) — working drafts (take, iterate in marketing):
- Short title (<= 60 chars): "Redwood Inference — Low-latency LLM API"
- Short description (<= 300 chars): "High-throughput LLM inference with predictable latency and flexible deployment options — hosted API, reserved capacity, and private VPC deployments. Integrated cost controls and monitoring for production workloads."
- Long description (working): "Redwood Inference provides a production-grade inference platform built for engineering teams. Ship LLM features faster with consistent latency and predictable unit economics. Choose hosted, dedicated, or private deployments with built-in rollout controls, caching, and model recommendations. Includes telemetry, token-level cost breakdowns, and intuitive APIs for text generation, chat, embeddings and reranking. Ideal for product teams needing SLAs, security controls, and enterprise observability.\nUse cases:\n • Assistant & chat features at scale\n • Document search and semantic retrieval\n • High-throughput embedding generation\n• Reranking and personalization at low-latency\n\nFeature bullets (for tile):\n• Predictable per-token latency and autoscaling\n• Dedicated GPU pools and private deployment options\n• Cost controls: batching, KV cache, quantization suggestions\n• Rollouts: canary, A/B, automatic fallbacks\n• Observability: token-level cost/latency and tracing hooks\n\nSample tile prompts & responses (trim to ~1–2 lines each):\n- Prompt: "Summarize the latest developer notes about pricing."\n  Response (example): "Redwood’s Optimize tool suggests batching and a 4-bit quantization for embeddings to reduce unit cost by ~35% while preserving quality."\n- Prompt: "Find customer intent from this support ticket: 'login failing after SSO'"\n  Response: "Likely SSO config mismatch; ask for full error trace and user-id; recommend re-run of SSO metadata import."\n\nLegal copy (short):\n- Trial: 14-day free trial. Usage recorded for metering. See full terms at https://legal.redwood.ai/marketplace-trial\n- Data handling: Customer data processed per agreed DPA and retention policy."

Acceptance criteria for publish (final gated checklist):
- All preflight boxes checked by owner + partner (owner signs off in ticket).
- Demo executed and recorded, meeting notes attached to publish ticket.
- Support playbook created (1-pager) and linked.
- Billing reconciliation test green (test invoice generated).
- Legal signoff present.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self style):
- Should we expose a per-product free-tier (0–1k tokens/month) on marketplace? Pros/cons: easier trial vs. meter reconciliation friction. (Follow-up: GTM-sync 2025-02-05)
- Need final alt-text for two screenshots. @Riley to add by end of week.
- Confirm backup SLA: is 500ms degraded latency acceptable for U.S. enterprise partners? Create SRE ticket: SRE-351.

Meeting log snippets (internal, informal):
- 2024-11-12 standup: Marcus flagged a mismatch between meter IDs and our telemetry -> fixed mapping in PR #61.
- 2024-12-03 partner call: partner wants a monthly commitment SKU; asked to scope reserved capacity offer.

How to use this doc:
- SEs: follow preflight checklist verbatim prior to scheduled demo. Mark items 'done' in Jira GTM-9473 and attach evidence (screenshots, logs).
- PMs: iterate on copy in the long_description field; tag marketing for final polish.
- Ops: run capacity failover test during demo and post demo as a staged-sanity check.

Revision history (brief):
- 2024-11-08: initial draft (Ava)
- 2024-12-10: added metering mapping and sample prompts (Marcus)
- 2025-01-29: clarified acceptance criteria and demo timeline (Riley)

Quick links (for SE during demo):
- Provisioning playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/MP-PROV-PLAYBOOK
- Billing mapping sheet: https://sheets.redwood.ai/d/marketplace-billing-mapping
- Slack channel: #gcm-marketplace-onboard

Notes to self: keep this lean — partners get overwhelmed with >2 lists. Keep one actionable checklist and one copy slate.

End.
